Spanish insurer Mapfre estimated losses from the June 24 earthquakes at €25 million, as reported in a new financial update. Meanwhile, a local story highlights false hope from fake news about survivors, and a grandfather continues searching for his missing grandson.
As of July 24, one month after the twin earthquakes, the death toll tops 5,300 with tens of thousands still missing and residents conducting their own searches as government clearance threatens to proceed before families recover loved ones. Reports highlight how poverty divides even in death, with the poor disproportionately affected, and Venezuela's inability to access $4 billion in gold reserves hampers recovery efforts.
One month after the twin earthquakes, family members and volunteers continue desperate searches through rubble, with the confirmed death toll reported at over 5,300. Relief efforts from organizations like GEM in South Florida persist, while local and international media highlight the ongoing challenges of rebuilding and recovery.
Twin earthquakes in Venezuela caused at least $19.6 billion in direct physical damage, according to World Bank estimates. The country's healthcare system is facing unprecedented strain as thousands are injured and displaced, with international aid organizations struggling to cope. An AP photo captured a mother's anguish as families searched through collapsed buildings for survivors.
A new report criticizes Venezuela's emergency response, suggesting many of the over 5,000 deaths could have been avoided with professional efforts in the first 72 hours. Global Empowerment Mission is expanding into a second phase of earthquake relief. Additionally, insurer Mapfre estimated losses at €25 million, and CNN reported on hundreds of rescued pets seeking reunification with their families.

New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

logs.summary:
A massive wildfire in central Spain has burned over 32,000 hectares (79,000 acres), becoming one of the country's largest on record, forcing thousands to evacuate. The Spanish government declared a national emergency on July 24 as the blaze continued to rage. Three firefighters died in associated wildfires across Europe, with two in France and one in Italy, while Spain's annual wildfire average was crossed before August.
Spain declared its first-ever national emergency as wildfires near Madrid and Avila forced 20,000 evacuations, while in southwestern France over 60,000 people, including tourists, were evacuated from the Cap Ferret peninsula by boat. Both countries requested assistance from the European Union as the fires, fueled by a marine heatwave and extreme temperatures, burned over 100 square kilometers in France.
The total number of evacuees from wildfires in Spain and France has risen to over 90,000, with 40,000 people ordered to evacuate or shelter in the Madrid region alone. A major wildfire in southern France near Cap Ferret is now reported to be under control, though blazes continue to rage in central Spain. Authorities are deploying novel firefighting methods, including using donkeys to graze flammable vegetation.

logs.summary:
By July 24-25, wildfires in southwestern France and central Spain forced over 200,000 people to evacuate, with France reporting 141,000 evacuees from the Gironde and Landes departments and Spain evacuating 60,000. French President Emmanuel Macron ordered military mobilization as a blaze approached the city of Bordeaux, while Spain's national emergency declaration covered the Madrid region and Avila province. Dozens of firefighters were injured but no deaths were reported.
On July 25, 2026, about 20,000 people were evacuated from towns along the French Atlantic coast as a wildfire spread, while around 197,000 evacuations were ordered in the Gironde and Landes regions. France prepared an A400M aircraft to drop retardant on the Gironde wildfire near Bordeaux, and evacuations also occurred near Madrid in Spain as blazes continued.
By July 25, the total number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 267,000, with France evacuating suburbs of Bordeaux as a massive wildfire shifts toward the city. France deployed a specially adapted A400M cargo aircraft to dump flame retardants on the blaze, and French President Macron stated the country "will rebuild" after the fires. Officials described the Madrid wildfire as the "worst fire in the history of the region" and the final stage of the Tour de France was shortened due to the fires.

logs.summary:
New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

logs.summary:
A wildfire erupted in the historic Fontainebleau forest south of Paris, burning over 2,000 hectares and prompting the evacuation of about 1,000 residents. French authorities arrested two people suspected of deliberately starting the blaze, while hundreds of firefighters and waterbombing aircraft worked to contain the fire as Europe faced another heatwave.

The wildfires in the Fontainebleau forest have shown mixed status: some reports indicate containment, while others report the fire is still spreading with 850 firefighters and 200 vehicles deployed. Authorities discovered ten ignition points and arrested two suspects on suspicion of arson.

On July 15, approximately 800 firefighters continued to tackle flare-ups in the Fontainebleau forest as French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to replant the historic forest. Meanwhile, authorities are investigating a volunteer firefighter as a suspect in starting the devastating blaze, which burned over 2,000 hectares near Paris.

Reports varied on the exact death toll, with some sources citing up to six deaths and 32 injuries.
